population_description: Large volunteer cohort with deep phenotyping, biomarkers, linked health records, imaging and genetics.
approx_population: ~500,000 enrolled; multiple published Lp(a) analyses >300,000
key_strengths: Very large measured-Lp(a) sample; genetics; imaging; long follow-up; rich cardiovascular phenotypes.
key_limitations: Volunteer cohort; UK generalizability; limited payer/cost detail; assay harmonization needs.
published_lpa_example: Patel et al. 2020; Bhatia et al. 2025; multiple 2026 UK Biobank Lp(a) studies.

population_description: Diverse U.S. participant cohort integrating EHR, surveys, biospecimens, physical measures and genomics.
approx_population: 266,612 adults with EHR in published Lp(a) analysis; program designed for >1 million participants
key_strengths: Diverse U.S. cohort; EHR + SDOH + genomics; direct proof of Lp(a) testing in mg/dL and nmol/L.
key_limitations: Lp(a) testing sparse; EHR incompleteness; volunteer/convenience sample.
published_lpa_example: Prevalence and Correlates of Lp(a) Testing in a Diverse Cohort of U.S. Adults, JACC: Advances, 2025.

population_description: Multi-ethnic prospective cohort focused on subclinical and clinical cardiovascular disease.
approx_population: ~6,800 enrolled; 6,670 with Lp(a) in 2025 PREVENT analysis
key_strengths: Deep CVD phenotyping, imaging, diversity, long-term outcomes, measured Lp(a).
key_limitations: Smaller than EHR/claims networks; not designed for contemporary cost analyses.
published_lpa_example: Bhatia et al., JAMA Cardiology 2025; Mehta et al., JACC 2024 pooled cohort.

population_description: Long-running prospective study of cardiovascular risk and outcomes in U.S. communities.
approx_population: ~15,000 original cohort; contributes Lp(a) data to pooled U.S. analyses
key_strengths: Long follow-up, rich CVD phenotyping, Lp(a), genetics and major cardiovascular outcomes.
key_limitations: Historical cohort/assays; limited contemporary prescribing, payer and cost data.
published_lpa_example: Mehta et al., JACC 2024 pooled cohort; Nomura et al., JAHA 2025.

population_description: Prospective cohort beginning in young adulthood with repeated cardiovascular risk-factor examinations.
approx_population: ~5,100 original cohort; contributes Lp(a) data to 27,756-person pooled analysis
key_strengths: Life-course perspective, racial diversity, repeated phenotyping and long follow-up.
key_limitations: Modest sample size; historical measurements; little direct cost/claims detail.
published_lpa_example: Mehta et al., JACC 2024 pooled multi-ethnic prospective cohort.

population_description: Longitudinal offspring cohort with repeated cardiovascular examinations and event follow-up.
approx_population: ~5,100 original offspring; thousands with historical Lp(a) measures
key_strengths: Exceptionally long follow-up, detailed CVD phenotyping and historical Lp(a) assay documentation.
key_limitations: Historically less diverse; older assay eras; limited contemporary utilization/cost data.
published_lpa_example: Lamon-Fava et al. 2011; Mehta et al. JACC 2024.

population_description: Long-term community-based cohort of more than 5,300 African American adults.
approx_population: >5,300 enrolled
key_strengths: Purpose-built Black cardiovascular cohort; rich SDOH, genomics and longitudinal phenotyping.
key_limitations: Regional cohort; modest size; not designed for contemporary claims/cost analyses.
published_lpa_example: Li et al., Journal of Human Genetics 2015; Mehta et al., JACC 2024.

geographic_scope: All 50 U.S. states plus participating international sites
population_description: Large EHR-derived network from Epic health systems, used for national Lp(a) testing analyses.
approx_population: >300 million patient records in 2025 Lp(a) publication
key_strengths: Huge scale, current clinical testing behavior, geography/demographics, both mass and molar units.
key_limitations: Access is governed; EHR completeness and outcome validation vary; limited direct costs.
published_lpa_example: Ramsis et al., JACC: Advances 2025.

population_description: Federated clinical network supporting aggregate cohort queries and observational analyses.
approx_population: 123,234,330 U.S. adults in 2026 Lp(a) testing analysis
key_strengths: Very large scale; rapid cohort feasibility; measured Lp(a), outcomes and medications.
key_limitations: Site heterogeneity; variable completeness; limited cost detail; assay metadata may be incomplete.
published_lpa_example: Kassab & Harb, JACC 2026 nationwide TriNetX analysis.

source_name: Optum Clinformatics Data Mart + laboratory data
population_description: Longitudinal medical and pharmacy claims with eligibility data; a subset has laboratory results.
approx_population: Large insured U.S. population; published Lp(a) study notes lab data for ~30% in database environment
key_strengths: Claims + pharmacy + eligibility + utilization/costs with Lp(a) laboratory subset.
key_limitations: Insured population; labs only for subset; limited genetics/clinical depth.
published_lpa_example: Characteristics and lipid lowering treatment patterns in patients tested for Lp(a), 2023.

organization: Family Heart Foundation; source data from Symphony Health / ICON
data_type: Longitudinal medical claims + linked laboratory data
population_description: U.S. individuals with longitudinal medical-claims activity; enriched for lipid-disorder and cardiovascular-risk research
approx_population: ~340 million individuals in source database; 1,232,206 with ≥1 Lp(a) result in nmol/L and 46,059 in mg/dL
key_strengths: Very large national claims footprint; linked laboratory data; >1.2M people with Lp(a) in nmol/L; long longitudinal observation; medication, diagnosis, procedure, and surgery coding; assay characteristics documented in published Lp(a) work.
key_limitations: Cost and payer fields were not established from the reviewed publication; claims-derived clinical detail is limited; laboratory availability applies to only a subset of the source population.
published_lpa_example: Lipoprotein(a) and recurrent atherosclerotic cardiovascular events: the US Family Heart Database (European Heart Journal, 2025)

source_name: HealthVerity linked claims + laboratory + mortality data
data_type: Closed medical and pharmacy claims + deterministically linked laboratory and mortality data
population_description: Deidentified U.S. individuals represented in closed medical/pharmacy claims with linked laboratory and mortality data
approx_population: >240 million individuals in source data; 731,983 in published Lp(a) derivation cohort
key_strengths: Closed medical and pharmacy claims linked to cholesterol laboratory and mortality data; very large U.S. scale; strong fit for longitudinal ASCVD outcomes and treatment-pattern analyses.
key_limitations: Published Lp(a) paper does not establish cost fields, full payer detail, genomics, or imaging availability; laboratory linkage and assay detail require protocol-specific verification.
published_lpa_example: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Independently Increases Risk for Short-Term Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Events in Machine Learning Predictive Models (JACC: Advances, 2025)

data_type: Linked electronic health record + medical/pharmacy claims
population_description: Deidentified linked EHR and claims data; used as an independent validation cohort in published Lp(a) research
approx_population: 53,930 individuals with Lp(a) measurements in published validation cohort
key_strengths: Links EHR clinical detail with claims; demonstrated Lp(a) availability in a 53,930-person validation cohort; potentially strong for outcomes, treatment, utilization, and HEOR questions.
key_limitations: The reviewed Lp(a) publication does not fully document cost-field completeness, payer granularity, mortality capture, assay characteristics, or imaging availability; these require product-level verification.
published_lpa_example: Independent EHR + linked-claims validation cohort in Ward et al., JACC: Advances (2025)
verification_status: Verified from peer-reviewed publication; some capabilities provisional

population_description: Patients with elevated Lp(a), defined as ≥100 nmol/L (≥50 mg/dL), followed prospectively
approx_population: Not established from the abstract reviewed
key_strengths: Lp(a)-specific prospective longitudinal registry; baseline and annual collection of demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, laboratory results, and clinical outcomes.
key_limitations: Not designed as a claims/HEOR database; published design abstract does not establish payer, utilization, cost, genetics, imaging, race/ethnicity, or detailed medication capture.
published_lpa_example: Rationale and Design of the Canadian Lipoprotein(a) Registry (CJC Open, 2026)
verification_status: Verified from published registry-design article; detailed fields pending

data_type: Distributed multi-health-system EHR network / common data model
geographic_scope: National U.S.; >50 million people represented annually
population_description: Patients receiving routine care across participating U.S. health systems; data standardized to the PCORnet Common Data Model
approx_population: >50 million people represented annually; published Lp(a) study included 20,551 adults with Lp(a) results across 11 health systems
key_strengths: National distributed EHR network with standardized labs, prescribing/dispensing, diagnoses, procedures, encounters, mortality, and race/ethnicity. Published Lp(a) work directly evaluated testing, treatment initiation, and CV hospitalizations.
key_limitations: Capabilities vary by Network Partner; payer, SDOH, imaging, biobank/genetic linkage and dispensing completeness are not uniform. Published Lp(a) analysis used 11 selected systems.
published_lpa_example: Contemporary patterns of lipoprotein(a) testing and associated clinical care and outcomes (Am J Prev Cardiol, 2023)
verification_status: Verified from peer-reviewed Lp(a) publication + PCORnet documentation

organization: University of Alabama at Birmingham / NIH-supported investigators
geographic_scope: 48 contiguous U.S. states + DC; Stroke Belt and Black participants oversampled
population_description: 30,239 Black and White adults aged ≥45 enrolled 2003–2007 for study of geographic and racial differences in stroke
approx_population: 30,239 overall; multiple Lp(a) case-cohort subsets
key_strengths: Large national prospective cohort designed for racial/geographic disparity research; rigorous adjudication of stroke/CHD; medication reconciliation, blood samples, socioeconomic data, and documented Lp(a) assays.
key_limitations: Lp(a) measured in nested subsets rather than entire cohort; Black and White adults only; not a claims/cost database; proposal and IRB/DUA governance required.
published_lpa_example: Lp(a) and Risk of Ischemic Stroke in REGARDS (ATVB, 2019); secondary-prevention analysis (JAHA, 2022)
verification_status: Verified from peer-reviewed publications + study access documentation

population_description: Multiethnic probability sample enriched for Black participants with deep cardiovascular phenotyping
approx_population: ~3,500 phenotyped participants; 2,078 with both Lp(a) and CAC in published outcomes analysis
key_strengths: Deep multiethnic phenotyping with Lp(a), apo(a) isoforms/genetic information and cardiovascular imaging including coronary artery calcium; longitudinal ASCVD outcomes.
key_limitations: Regional cohort with modest sample size; not routine-care EHR/claims; no dispensing or cost data; less suited to treatment-pattern or utilization research.
published_lpa_example: Independent Association of Lp(a) and CAC with ASCVD Risk: MESA and Dallas Heart Study (JACC, 2022)

data_type: Prospective general-population cohort with national registry linkage
population_description: Large contemporary Danish general-population cohort recruited from 2003 onward
approx_population: 109,440 in a published analysis; 70,286 with plasma Lp(a), 99,328 with LPA KIV-2 genotype and 108,511 with key LPA SNP genotypes
key_strengths: Very large prospective population cohort with extensive Lp(a) measurement, LPA genotyping, essentially complete national registry follow-up, and broad cardiovascular/mortality endpoints.
key_limitations: Predominantly Danish population limits some diversity questions; not a U.S. claims/payer database; cost and insurance questions are not a core strength.
published_lpa_example: Low lipoprotein(a) levels and risk of disease in a large contemporary general population study (Eur Heart J, 2021)

data_type: Prospective population-based cohort with national registry linkage
population_description: General-population cohort with repeated examination waves and long national-registry follow-up
approx_population: ~9,000–11,000 in major Lp(a) analyses; follow-up extending decades
key_strengths: Decades of prospective follow-up, Lp(a) and LPA genotype data, and national-registry ascertainment of MI, stroke, HF, aortic stenosis and mortality.
key_limitations: Smaller and less diverse than modern national biobanks; not a claims/cost source; treatment and utilization capture is secondary to epidemiologic use.
published_lpa_example: Extreme Lp(a) levels and risk of myocardial infarction in the general population (Circulation, 2008)

data_type: Harmonized European prospective-cohort consortium with central biomarker laboratory
population_description: Harmonized population-based cohorts with centrally stored biomaterial and standardized biomarker measurement
approx_population: >300,000 participants represented in consortium; 56,804 participants from 7 cohorts in published Lp(a) analysis, 52,131 with Lp(a)
key_strengths: Cross-country European harmonization, central laboratory Lp(a) measurement using the same assay, long follow-up, and standardized cardiovascular risk variables.
key_limitations: Consortium rather than a single routine-care database; cohort variables/access differ; not suited to payer, cost, or routine Lp(a)-testing-pattern analyses.
published_lpa_example: Lp(a) and cardiovascular disease risk in the European population: BiomarCaRE consortium (Eur Heart J, 2017)

organization: Brigham and Women's Hospital / Harvard Medical School investigators
data_type: Prospective cohort derived from a randomized primary-prevention trial
population_description: Initially healthy U.S. women followed prospectively for cardiovascular outcomes
approx_population: 27,791 with baseline Lp(a) in a 2006 analysis; 24,558 in a 2018 risk-prediction analysis
key_strengths: Large prospective primary-prevention cohort with baseline Lp(a) measured using an apo(a)-isoform-independent assay and long cardiovascular follow-up; recent analyses extend follow-up to 30 years.
key_limitations: Women only; not a routine-care EHR/claims source; no cost or dispensing data; historical cohort design limits use for current testing-pattern questions.
published_lpa_example: Lipoprotein(a), measured with an assay independent of apo(a) isoform size, and risk of future cardiovascular events among initially healthy women (JAMA, 2006)

data_type: Prospective observational cohort with adjudicated outcomes and selected Medicare linkage
population_description: Postmenopausal U.S. women enrolled in the WHI Observational Study
approx_population: 93,676 in WHI Observational Study overall; Lp(a) available in nested/case-cohort subsets, including 1,815 CVD cases + 1,989 subcohort in a 2018 analysis
key_strengths: Large national prospective study of postmenopausal women with rich demographic and socioeconomic data, adjudicated cardiovascular outcomes, measured Lp(a) in multiple ancillary studies, and Medicare claims linkage in eligible participants.
key_limitations: Lp(a) is not uniformly measured across the full cohort; women only and postmenopausal; Medicare linkage applies to subsets and does not make WHI a general-purpose claims database.
published_lpa_example: Lipoprotein(a) and Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Among Women (JACC, 2018); Lp(a) and AAA risk in WHI with Medicare linkage (2020)

population_description: Initially healthy middle-aged and older men and women from the general population
approx_population: 18,720 with Lp(a) in a 2012 vascular-outcomes analysis; 17,087 in a 2025 20-year MACE analysis
key_strengths: Prospective European population cohort with measured Lp(a), detailed baseline risk factors, and long follow-up for CAD, stroke, PAD and MACE; 2025 work provides 20-year primary-prevention validation.
key_limitations: Regional UK cohort; not a routine-care testing or claims source; limited payer/cost utility and less diverse than U.S. multiethnic cohorts.
published_lpa_example: Lp(a) and risk of coronary, cerebrovascular, and peripheral artery disease (ATVB, 2012); universal one-time screening analysis (Eur Heart J, 2025)

data_type: Population genetics + measured/imputed biomarker data + linked disease phenotypes
population_description: Large Icelandic population genetics resource with measured and genetically imputed Lp(a), LPA variants, and linked disease phenotypes
approx_population: 143,087 Icelanders with genetic information in a 2020 Lp(a) analysis
key_strengths: Exceptional LPA genetic resolution, measured and genetically imputed molar Lp(a), very large population sample, and linked cardiovascular phenotypes including CAD, PAD, aortic valve stenosis, heart failure and lifespan.
key_limitations: Genetically homogeneous Icelandic population; proprietary/governed access; not suited to routine-care testing, treatment-pattern, payer, cost, or utilization research.
published_lpa_example: Lipoprotein(a) Concentration and Risks of Cardiovascular Disease and Diabetes (JACC, 2020)

organization: Brigham and Women's Hospital / Harvard investigators
data_type: Prospective cohort derived from randomized primary-prevention trial
population_description: Predominantly White male U.S. physicians initially free of major cardiovascular disease
approx_population: 14,916 men provided baseline plasma samples in a prospective Lp(a)-stroke analysis
key_strengths: Prospective biospecimen cohort with adjudicated cardiovascular follow-up and historical Lp(a) analyses.
key_limitations: Predominantly White male physicians, limiting generalizability and equity applications; older cohort; not a routine-care, claims, cost or utilization source.
published_lpa_example: Plasma concentration of lipoprotein(a) and the risk of future stroke (JAMA, 1995)
